name: Pelleve
lead: Pellevé is a monopolar radiofrequency wrinkle-treatment system made by Ellman International, operating at 4 MHz [1][2]. It was one of the RF devices that followed the introduction of Thermage in 2002 [4].

Published studies include a 17-patient facial study [1], a 31-patient hand-wrinkle study [2] and a 12-patient periorbital cohort [3]. A 2011 clinical article describes the procedure as delivering continuous monopolar RF energy and repeatedly bringing skin to therapeutic temperatures until maximal contraction is obtained [4].

paras: Pellevé delivers continuous monopolar RF rather than pulsed heating; the 2011 article authors describe the approach as treating all areas until contraction is seen and as comfortable for patients [4]. A 2012 paper reviews the science of RF-induced collagen synthesis alongside its clinical series [1].

The 2012 study of 17 patients receiving a series of 4-MHz monopolar RF facial treatments is reported in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology [1]. A multicenter study enrolled 31 women with a median age of 56 for hand wrinkles and described itself as the first to assess hand laxity improvement with RF [2]. A prospective cohort of 12 patients used a Canfield imaging system to document periorbital wrinkle change after one or two sessions [3]. All are small studies without a described control arm.

Studies are described above [1][2][3][4]. ClinicalTrials.gov lists a 40-participant study of single versus double and triple Pellevé therapy for facial wrinkles (started 2010) [5] and a 49-participant neck wrinkle study (2010) [6]; results are not summarised here.

timeline.event: Thermage introduced, beginning the market for nonablative RF skin heating devices.[4]

card.summary: Ellman's 4-MHz monopolar RF system for wrinkles and tightening, backed by small uncontrolled studies.
card.note: Studies are small and mostly without control groups.

quick.overview:
Pellevé is a clinic-based monopolar radiofrequency system from Ellman International used for facial and neck wrinkles and, in one study, hand wrinkles.

Published work is limited to small studies of 12 to 31 patients.
quick.mechanism: Continuous 4-MHz radiofrequency energy heats skin to therapeutic temperature, with the aim of contracting collagen and stimulating new collagen.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give little safety detail; category-wide RF reports include pain, burns, pigment change and rare scarring or fat loss.
